record.paper_title: Some open problems on the classical function space L1
record.original_question: Is every projection P on L1[0,1] that is L1-singular, meaning that it does not fix any subspace isomorphic to L1[0,1], necessarily a Dunford-Pettis operator?

evidence.quote: Problem 13. ([107], [31] and [9]) Is every L1-singular projection P ∈ L(L1) a Dunford-Pettis operator?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L_1 := L_1[0,1]$ denote the Banach space of (equivalence classes of) Lebesgue integrable real-valued functions on $[0,1]$ with the norm $\|f\|_1 = \int_0^1 |f(t)|\,dt$. A bounded linear operator $T \in \mathcal{L}(L_1)$ is called:

(i) $L_1$-singular if there is no closed subspace $X \subseteq L_1$ isomorphic to $L_1$ such that $T|_X$ is an isomorphism onto its image (equivalently, $T$ does not fix a copy of $L_1$);

(ii) a Dunford–Pettis operator (also called completely continuous) if $T$ maps weakly null sequences to norm null sequences, i.e., whenever $f_n \to 0$ weakly in $L_1$, one has $\|Tf_n\|_1 \to 0$.

A projection on $L_1$ is an operator $P \in \mathcal{L}(L_1)$ with $P^2 = P$.

Question: Is every $L_1$-singular projection $P \in \mathcal{L}(L_1)$ a Dunford–Pettis operator?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not yield a definitive resolution of this specific question. The literature contains substantial work on Dunford–Pettis operators on $L_1$ and on operators that fix or fail to fix copies of $L_1$, but no source found in the search explicitly resolves whether every $L_1$-singular projection on $L_1[0,1]$ must be a Dunford–Pettis operator. The status is therefore reported as unknown based on available evidence.

status_evidence.claim: Provides background definitions but does not resolve the specific projection question.

status_evidence.claim: Recent literature on related operator classes does not announce a resolution of the L1-singular projection question.
